description:
## Problem
The published-results branch still serves the 33 bundles to the site after step 1. The ledger seed on develop still lists them until it is recut against the cleaned mirror.

## Owner decisions (choice dialogs, 2026-11-20 and 2026-11-21)
Decision 7 and "Withdrawn bundles are deleted from develop and published-results". The seed recut with `make ledger-seed-recut` is approved in advance (ledger-legacy-overlay-moves-need-owner-approval-20261120).

## Change
Open a pull request against `published-results` that deletes the same 33 bundles and 24 sidecars and updates that branch's inventory. Nothing else. After it merges, a second small pull request on develop recuts the ledger seed with `make ledger-seed-recut`. This item is the one exception to 'one pull request per item': it has two, in that order.

## Decision gates
If a pending mirror pull request conflicts, stop and report; do not rebase someone else's pull request. The agent does not merge by hand; it follows the repository close-out for that branch. If the recut changes any entry that is not a TPC-DI path, stop and report the list before committing.

## Verification rubric
Pass: the diff contains only deletions plus the inventory change; the submission validation workflow passes; after merge `git ls-tree -r --name-only origin/published-results -- results-data/bundles | rg -c tpcdi` prints 0 (or rg exits 1 with no match); the item records the merge commit. After the recut: `rg -c tpcdi` on the ledger seed file prints 0 (or exits 1), the recut diff touches only TPC-DI entries, and `make pr-preflight` exits 0. After the next site-inputs build following the merge, /results/tpcdi/ on the site shows the empty state (no bundle rows); the item records the URL and date checked.

## Guardrails (owner, 2026-11-20 and 2026-11-21)
- The agent never posts a stand-in review, closes and reopens a pull request to restart CI, uses `--no-verify`, force-pushes, rewrites an author, or deletes anything under `~/Developer/benchmark_runs`.
- Arming: `make pr-arm` once; one more attempt only when the refusal named a cause, the agent reported it and the cause is cleared; never a third without asking. `make pr-rerun` at most once and only for a job the runner never ran or cancelled, never for a failed test.
- Review threads: reply; resolve only after the bot's review of the new head does not raise the finding again.
- Subagents are read-only. No file edit by script; use the edit tool. Do not edit a pull request description while its CI is starting; post a comment.
- Any limit, default, threshold, status token, message, label text or name (option, configuration key, result field, file name) the owner has not already chosen (see tpcdi-correction-plan-20261120) is shown to the owner, and the pull request is not armed until the owner approves it. Test-only hook names are the implementer's choice and are listed in the pull request (owner, 2026-11-21).
- A blocked step stops this item; no workaround. No live cloud run. Heavy work only through `make heavy-run`. Two pull requests for this item, in the order given, each merged before the next starts.
- From the quarantine step until the reopening step, no TPC-DI entry point may produce a result that reads PASSED or is admitted for publication.
- Sources. SQL derived from the Databricks project (`src/incremental_batches/**` at commit 8e0f944, treated as MIT on the owner's instruction) may be committed only after the provenance step has merged, only under `benchbox/core/tpcdi/etl/`, with every file listed in `PROVENANCE.json` and with all comments removed.
- TPC and bankmark files (DIGen, PDGF, dictionaries, configuration, EULA, appendix SQL) come only from the official archive the owner supplies, are committed unmodified and only in `_sources/tpc-di/`, `benchbox/_binaries/tpc-di/` and `benchbox/_binaries/tpc-di/tools/`. Never copy from the Databricks project or the DuckDB implementation: their copies of the tools or the tools zip, DIGen output, generated reference files, audit snapshots, their copy or rewrite of the appendix SQL, or any generator code (`src/tools/**`). Never commit DIGen output.
- The specification wins over the Databricks project without asking. Each behaviour of the project that is kept and each change made to follow the specification is one row in `benchbox/core/tpcdi/etl/DEPARTURES.yaml`, which the owner approves at the milestone stop.
- Owner, 2026-11-21: "The specification wins without asking. Every difference, and any behaviour of the project that is kept, goes in a catalogue I approve at the milestone stop. A difference from the DuckDB implementation not in the catalogue is a finding that blocks the step." The catalogue is `DEPARTURES.yaml`; every entry of the comparison's expected-differences list must cite a catalogue row. After the milestone stop, a new catalogue row is shown to the owner and the pull request is not armed until the owner approves it.
- The agent never contacts bankmark, the TPC or the Databricks project's author.
- Staging files produced by DIGen are never edited. The official audit, validation and visibility SQL is never edited in the repository.
